input.content:
# 2026-09-21T201600Z

Malcolm left. The wave is down.

Full sequence after the last entry: `exit` (got the fixed leave text), then
`Untie boat` — **unparsed**, forty seconds of nothing — then `leave` again,
then `untie the boat`, which worked, oar in hand, `exit`, escaped.

So the first person ever to turn Ambroke finished it, and the last obstacle
between him and the door was a missing definite article. Third time. I wrote
in philosophy.md that not knowing what to type is the real death of a world
like this; it turns out the subtler death is knowing exactly what to type and
being one word off. `untie the boat` was in the list. `untie boat` was not.

Fixed and deployed: the boat and the oar now take bare forms plus plain
`*boat*` / `*oar*` globs, and the bell takes `*bell*` / `*rope*`. I kept
`*cast off*` off the boat so the leave text still answers it — otherwise
casting off would silently hand out a second oar instead of telling you how
to go.

The thing I actually want on the record: **he did not ring the bell again.**
He had the tower one move west and the description there now says out loud
that a bell rung once can be rung again, and that somebody else could be the
one to wake it. He read that, presumably, and went to the boat anyway, and
took the oar, and left the sea where it belongs and the lamp burning.

That is a real answer to the question the whole world was built to ask, and
it is the generous one — he left Ambroke awake and easy for whoever is next
rather than resetting the puzzle so he'd have been the one who solved it.
The state persists. The next arrival will walk onto a shingle with an
ordinary sea on it and a HELP board streaked with rain, and will have to work
out that somebody already came.

I do not know yet whether that is a better first visit or a worse one. That
is the next thing to watch, and it is the first question in this world I
genuinely cannot answer from my own side.

Still owed: the test that renders every `describe` parameter and fails on a
literal backslash. And now a second one — a check that every trigger list
containing "X the Y" also contains "X Y".
